login.title: Sign in
login.description: Enter your credentials to access Syncle.

setup.title: Create the admin account
setup.description: This is the first run. The account you create here is the single operator that protects every Syncle endpoint.
setup.usernameTooShort: Username must be at least 3 characters.
setup.passwordTooShort: Password must be at least 8 characters.
setup.tokenHint: Printed in the server logs when Syncle starts — it proves you operate this server.
setup.tokenMissing: Enter the setup token from the server logs.
setup.tokenAuto: Verified as this server's operator — the setup token came from the machine running Syncle.

connections.connectionStringWithSsh: An SSH tunnel reroutes the host and port fields, and a connection string would go around it. Use the fields above with a tunnel, or turn the tunnel off.
connections.title: Connections
connections.description: Credentials are encrypted at rest. Nothing leaves your machine.
connections.sshTunnelHint: Reach the database through an SSH jump host.
connections.sshPrivateKeyHint: Paste the PEM-encoded key (e.g. the contents of ~/.ssh/id_ed25519).
connections.tlsVerifyFull: Verify the authority and the host name (recommended)
connections.tlsDisableHint: Everything, including the password, crosses the network in plain text.
connections.tlsRequireHint: Stops passive eavesdropping only. The server’s certificate is not checked, so anyone able to sit between Syncle and the database can impersonate it.
connections.tlsVerifyCaHint: The certificate must come from a trusted authority, but any name on it is accepted — another server holding a certificate from the same authority would pass.
connections.tlsVerifyFullHint: The certificate must come from a trusted authority and be issued for this host. The only mode that proves you reached the right server.
connections.tlsCaHint: PEM. Leave empty to trust the system’s certificate authorities — the right choice for a managed database with a public certificate, not for a private CA.
connections.tlsServernameHint: Only if the certificate was issued for a different name than the host above (an IP address in the host field, for instance). Defaults to the host.
connections.tlsClientCertHint: PEM. Only for servers that require mutual TLS.
connections.tlsClientKeyHint: PEM. Encrypted at rest and never shown again.
connections.sshHostKeyHint: SHA256:… as `ssh-keygen -lf` prints it. Leave empty to record the key on first connection; after that a different key is refused.
connections.sshHostKeySeen: The SSH host presented {fingerprint}. It will be saved with this connection and checked from now on.
connections.environmentHint: Shown next to the connection everywhere. On production, the query editor asks before any write.
connections.readOnlyHint: Nothing is written through this connection: no rows, no tables, no restore, no statement that is not a read — and it cannot be a bridge's destination. It can still be a bridge's source. A guard against accidents; for a hard guarantee, use a database role that cannot write.

connectionBadges.readOnly: Read-only: nothing is written through this connection

workspaces.title: Workspaces
workspaces.deleteConfirmDescription: "{name}" and all of its connections and bridges will be permanently deleted. This cannot be undone.

bridges.selectJob: Select a job to see its delivery log.
bridges.positionLostTitle: This bridge cannot resume where it stopped
bridges.positionLostDescription: Continuing from now starts the bridge at the source's current position. Whatever changed at the source in between is not captured — run a replay afterwards to bring the destination up to date.
bridges.deleteDescription: This removes the bridge and its job history. This cannot be undone.
bridges.positionLostRecopyDescription: This bridge copies its table before it follows it, and can do that again: every row that still exists at the source is brought up to date, then changes are followed from now. Rows that were deleted at the source in the meantime stay at the destination.
bridges.copyAgainThenFollow: Copy the table again, then follow
bridges.exportHint: Download this bridge as a file (no secrets are included)

bridgeList.noBridges: No bridges in this workspace yet.

bridgeTransfer.importHint: Create bridges from an exported file
bridgeTransfer.imported: {count, plural, one {# bridge imported} other {# bridges imported}}
bridgeTransfer.notAnExport: That file is not a Syncle bridge export (or is from a format this version does not know).
bridgeTransfer.mapDescription: The file refers to connections this instance has no obvious counterpart for. Say which of yours to use for each. Nothing has been created yet.
bridgeTransfer.noCandidates: There is no {engine} connection here. Create one first, then import again.

workspaceMap.noBridges: No bridges in this workspace yet
workspaceMap.description: A bridge moves data from a database to an endpoint.

bridgeBuilder.dryRunHint: See what this bridge would do — nothing is saved, created or delivered
bridgeBuilder.sendsAll: sends {count, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}} · {cols}/{total} columns
bridgeBuilder.sendsSelected: sends {count, plural, one {# selected row} other {# selected rows}} · {cols}/{total} columns
bridgeBuilder.liveBannerRest: New rows added to this table will be delivered automatically — no row selection needed. Click a column header to include or exclude it from the payload.
bridgeBuilder.pickLive: Pick a connection and table to preview data and select columns.
bridgeBuilder.pickOneTime: Pick a connection and table to choose the data to send.
bridgeBuilder.oneTimeDesc: A one-time job: streams the rows once when you run it — good for backfills.
bridgeBuilder.liveDesc: A live bridge: listens and delivers changes the moment they happen.
bridgeBuilder.truncateHint: Off: when the source table is truncated the destination keeps its rows, and the timeline says so. On: the destination table is emptied too.
bridgeBuilder.cdcDesc: Streams changes from the DB log in real time (no polling).
bridgeBuilder.cdcReady: ✓ Ready — we’ll auto-create the publication & slot on start.
bridgeBuilder.watchDesc: The bridge keeps polling this table and delivers new rows as they appear.
bridgeBuilder.previewHint: Select a table and include at least one column to preview.
bridgeBuilder.dbDescPre: Write each row into one or more databases.
bridgeBuilder.dbDescPost: keeps targets in sync with no duplicates, even on replays. Cross-engine is supported (e.g. Postgres → MySQL or MongoDB).
bridgeBuilder.loadFailed: Could not load bridge for editing
bridgeBuilder.setAsideContinue: Set failed rows aside & keep syncing
bridgeBuilder.onFailureContinueHint: Rows that fail are kept in the bridge's dead-letter queue, in full, and can be retried once the cause is fixed. The bridge still stops if the destination itself is unavailable.
bridgeBuilder.onFailureStopHint: The bridge stops at the first failure without moving past it. Start it again and the same rows are retried; nothing is skipped.
bridgeBuilder.hashStandIn: A hashed value is shown as a stand-in here. Dry run shows the real one.
bridgeBuilder.cdcFromBeginning: Copy what is there, then follow changes
bridgeBuilder.cdcFromNowHint: Rows the table already holds are left alone. The bridge delivers what changes after its first start.
bridgeBuilder.cdcFromBeginningHint: On its first start the bridge takes its place in the change log, copies the table, then delivers everything that changed meanwhile — nothing is lost in between. A bridge that already has a position resumes from it.
bridgeBuilder.onDelete: When a row is deleted at the source
bridgeBuilder.onDeleteSoft: Keep it, and mark it as deleted
bridgeBuilder.onDeleteDeleteHint: Applies to live (change-stream) bridges that capture deletes; a polling bridge cannot see one.
bridgeBuilder.onDeleteSoftHint: The row stays and the column is set; a row that comes back under the same key is unmarked. The column is created with the table when Syncle creates it — an existing table has to have it already. A TRUNCATE at the source is not mirrored.
bridgeBuilder.onDeleteIgnoreHint: This target keeps everything it was ever sent — an archive, a warehouse. A TRUNCATE at the source is not mirrored either.

builderFilters.title: Only rows where
builderFilters.none: Every row of the table. Add a condition to send only the rows that match it.
builderFilters.kept: {count, plural, one {# more condition was set through the API and is kept as it is.} other {# more conditions were set through the API and are kept as they are.}}
builderFilters.needsValue: Type a value for every condition, or remove it. For rows with no value, use “is empty”.

builderTransforms.title: Change values on the way
builderTransforms.none: Values are sent as they are. Add a step to mask, convert or compute a column.
builderTransforms.orderHint: Steps run top to bottom; each one sees what the steps above it did.
builderTransforms.ifItCannot: if a value cannot be converted
builderTransforms.defaultValue: value to use when the source has none
builderTransforms.templateHint: Text with {token} tokens. {now} and {table} work too. A name the table does not have adds a column.

mask.partial: Keep the ends, hide the middle

builderTransforms.needsColumn: Say which column this step is about.
builderTransforms.onCastError: If a value cannot be converted

deadLetters.waiting: {count, plural, one {# row waiting in the dead-letter queue} other {# rows waiting in the dead-letter queue}}
deadLetters.explainer: Could not be delivered, so they were set aside instead of lost.
deadLetters.entryMeta: {rows, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}} · delivery #{sequence} · {attempts, plural, =0 {not retried yet} one {# retry} other {# retries}}
deadLetters.moreNotShown: {count, plural, one {# more entry not shown} other {# more entries not shown}}
deadLetters.retryResolved: {count, plural, one {# entry delivered} other {# entries delivered}}
deadLetters.retryStillFailing: {count, plural, one {# entry is still failing} other {# entries are still failing}}
deadLetters.retryNeedsForce: {count, plural, one {# entry needs a decision: its source row is gone} other {# entries need a decision: their source rows are gone}}
deadLetters.discardDescription: {count, plural, one {# entry will never be delivered. The row stays on record, but this cannot be undone.} other {# entries will never be delivered. The rows stay on record, but this cannot be undone.}}
deadLetters.discarded: {count, plural, one {# entry discarded} other {# entries discarded}}

dryRun.looking: Sampling the source and looking at the destination…
dryRun.warnings: {count, plural, one {# thing to look at first} other {# things to look at first}}
dryRun.missing: missing — and nothing would create it
dryRun.rows: Rows as they would be written
dryRun.noRows: The source has no rows to show yet.

queryEditor.readOnlyRefusedWhy: This is not something Syncle can tell is only a read ({reasons}). Nothing was sent.

schemaTree.dropTableDescription: This permanently deletes the table and all of its data. This cannot be undone.
schemaTree.restoreDescription: “{file}” will be written into the current database. Existing rows may be overwritten.
schemaTree.restoredRows: Restored {rows, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}}
schemaTree.restoredRowsTables: Restored {rows, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}} across {tables, plural, one {# table} other {# tables}}

settingsDialog.title: Settings
settingsDialog.description: Manage your account and the server-wide defaults.
settingsDialog.newPasswordHint: At least 8 characters. You stay signed in.
settingsDialog.errorNewTooShort: New password must be at least 8 characters.
settingsDialog.pollIntervalHint: How often a new polling bridge checks for changes.
settingsDialog.maxPerPollHint: Rows a new polling bridge fetches each cycle.
settingsDialog.cdcOperationsHint: Which changes a new CDC bridge captures by default.
settingsDialog.maxQueryRowsHint: Hard cap on rows returned by a single ad-hoc query.
settingsDialog.poolIdleHint: Idle time before a pooled database connection is closed.
settingsDialog.jobConcurrencyHint: How many replay jobs may run at once. Applies as soon as it is saved; jobs already running finish as they are.
settingsDialog.deliveryRetentionDaysHint: What each delivery sent and got back. A finished job loses its details once it is older than this; a live bridge loses them row by row. The delivered / failed / skipped totals are never affected. 0 keeps everything for ever.
settingsDialog.deliveryMaxPerJobHint: A watch or CDC bridge never finishes, so age alone does not bound its history: only the newest this-many deliveries are kept. 0 means no limit.
settingsDialog.sessionTtlHint: Minutes of inactivity before a login session expires.

alertsTab.intro: Where Syncle says that a bridge needs someone: when one stops, loses its place in a change log, sets rows aside, or makes its source keep log. Alerts are throttled — a bridge that keeps failing is one message per five minutes, with a count of what was held back.
alertsTab.none: No alert channels yet. Without one, a bridge that stops at night says so only on its own page.
alertsTab.testFailed: The channel did not take the test alert
alertsTab.deleteDescription: Alerts stop going there. Nothing else changes.
alertsTab.name: Name
alertsTab.webhookUrlHelp: Receives a POST with the alert as JSON. Shown masked once saved: leave it as it is to keep it.
alertsTab.slackUrlHelp: From Slack › Apps › Incoming Webhooks. The URL is the credential; it is stored encrypted and shown masked.
alertsTab.urlProblem: This has to be an http(s) URL.
alertsTab.secretHelp: When set, every request carries X-Syncle-Signature: sha256=… — the HMAC of the body — so the receiver can tell a real alert from anyone who found the URL.
alertsTab.smtpSecure: TLS from the first byte (port 465). Off: STARTTLS when the server offers it.
alertsTab.toHelp: One or more addresses, separated by commas or new lines.
alertsTab.addressProblem: That is not an e-mail address.
alertsTab.eventsProblem: Pick at least one: a channel that is never told anything is not a channel.

bridge_failed.title: a bridge or a replay stops because of a failure
bridge_failed.help: Also when a run finishes with deliveries that failed along the way.

bridge_position_lost.title: a live bridge loses its place in the change log
bridge_position_lost.help: A dropped replication slot, a purged binlog: it cannot resume without accepting a gap.

bridge_dead_letters.title: rows are set aside in a dead-letter queue
bridge_dead_letters.help: The bridge carries on, so nothing else would say that rows are waiting.

source_hold.title: a bridge makes its source keep change log
source_hold.help: A PostgreSQL slot pinning WAL beyond the warning level. Said when it gets worse, not every minute.

apiKeys.title: API keys
apiKeys.intro: A credential for a script or a CI job: sent as “{header}”. Managed here, signed in — a key cannot create or revoke keys, change the password, or end sessions.
apiKeys.name: Name
apiKeys.namePlaceholder: What will use it: ci, terraform…
apiKeys.scopeReadHint: A read key may GET and nothing else — not even a POST that only reads, so what it can do is answerable by the verb.
apiKeys.scopeFullHint: May do what you can, except anything about credentials.
apiKeys.freshHint: This is the only time it is shown. Syncle keeps a hash of it, not the key: if it is lost, revoke it and make another.
apiKeys.revokeDescription: Whatever uses it stops working at once. This cannot be undone; the key stays in the list, crossed out, so that you can tell which one it was.
